title: PGA Tour announces 2028 two-tier structure; no return pathway for LIV players
dek: The PGA Tour announced a restructured membership model separating 114 Championship Series players from a Challenger Series, with eligibility determined by performance across 2026 and 2027. The Tour is rejecting any returning-member pathway for LIV defectors, insisting that all players, including major winners, must earn their way back through merit.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: The PGA Tour will not replicate the returning-member program offered to Brooks Koepka in January 2026, forcing LIV players seeking re-entry to compete for limited slots based on performance alone.
bottom_line: The number of DP World Tour cards allocated to the Championship Series versus Challenger Series will determine whether European players view the new structure as competitive or career-damaging. LIV's bankruptcy and the Tour's hard line on merit-only qualification will shape whether major players accept Challenger Series entry or remain outside the unified system.
body:
The PGA Tour announced a two-track membership structure starting in 2028, with 114 players in a Championship Series and a separate Challenger Series, determined by performance across the 2026 and 2027 seasons.
Tournaments will neither backfill nor hold alternate lists should a player withdraw, and no sponsor exemptions will be granted, per CBS Sports. Players will be eligible to compete in all Championship Series events, though the Masters, PGA Championship, U.S. Open, Open Championship, and The Players Championship may maintain their own criteria.
LIV filed for bankruptcy protection last week, according to the BBC and the Guardian, leaving the business seeking to launch a 2.0 version. The timing has prompted major players to reconsider their futures. According to the BBC, Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau, and Cameron Smith are contemplating their futures after the bankruptcy filing. Rahm told the BBC: "There's a long legal process they have to go through before a lot of things fall into place. I really can't give you an answer right now."
The new structure creates friction with the DP World Tour. According to the Guardian, Rory McIlroy said: "I don't see any reason why a DP World Tour player would go to the Challenger Series. I don't see that as an upward move in your career. I see it as a very lateral move." The Guardian reports that Rolapp said: "We have not determined what the DP World Tour cards will be, as of yet. That's under discussion. I don't see any scenarios where there's no Championship Series cards." Currently, the leading 10 finishers on the Race to Dubai earn PGA Tour cards, per BBC Sport, but that arrangement may change.
